name: LPS25HBTR
title: MEMS absolute pressure sensor, 260-1260 hPa, digital output barometer
summary: The LPS25HB is a piezoresistive MEMS absolute pressure sensor with an interface chip that compensates for temperature and gives 24-bit pressure and 16-bit temperature readings over I²C or SPI. It covers 260 to 1260 hPa, runs from 1.7 to 3.6 V and draws a few microamps at 1 Hz. It has a 32-slot FIFO, a hardware moving average, a differential-pressure threshold interrupt and a data-ready output. It comes in a holed 2.5 x 2.5 mm HLGA-10L package and operates from -30 to +105 °C.

I²C to 400 kHz, SPI to 10 MHz

circuits.title: Electrical connections
circuits.description: The sensor wired for either bus. VDD feeds pin 10 with a 100 nF capacitor, C1, close to the supply pads; pins 8 and 9 and the reserved pin 3 go to ground. Vdd_IO supplies the interface pins. Clock is on pin 2, data on pin 4, SDO or address bit SA0 on pin 5, CS on pin 6 and the interrupt output on pin 7. CS high (tied to Vdd_IO) picks I²C; CS low picks SPI.

parts.note: VDD decoupling, at the supply pads

notes: A further 4.7 µF on the VDD line may be added, depending on the application.
In I²C, CS goes to Vdd_IO and SDA and SCL each need a pull-up to Vdd_IO.

where.PRESS_OUT: 24-bit two's-complement count in registers 2Ah (high byte), 29h and 28h (low byte)

where.THS_P: 16-bit unsigned value, high byte in 31h, low byte in 30h

operation.text: A silicon membrane carries a piezoresistive Wheatstone bridge; pressure bends the membrane and unbalances the bridge. A low-noise front end and ADC convert the bridge signal and an on-chip temperature sensor reading to numbers, and the result is compensated for temperature before it reaches the I²C/SPI interface. The package top is holed so outside air reaches the membrane.

Each part is trimmed at two pressures, each at three temperatures. The trim values live in non-volatile memory and load into registers at power-up, and the part works without further calibration. A one-point calibration after soldering (OPC) is supported through the RPDS offset registers.

VDD powers the device and needs 100 nF as near its pads as possible, with 4.7 µF more optional. All supplies and grounds must be up together for correct behaviour. VDD may be removed with Vdd_IO kept: the measurement chain turns off and the bus is not blocked.

I²C and SPI share pins. CS high (to Vdd_IO) selects I²C; CS low selects SPI. The I²C block can also be switched off with I2C_DIS in CTRL_REG2. SPI runs 4-wire by default and 3-wire with SIM = 1 in CTRL_REG1, where pin 4 carries data both ways.

The 7-bit slave address is 101110x: SA0 (pin 5) high gives 1011101 (5Dh), low gives 1011100 (5Ch), so two parts can share a bus. The part is a slave for standard (100 kHz) and fast (400 kHz) mode, and SDA and SCL need pull-ups to Vdd_IO. After the address byte comes the sub-address byte: bits 6-0 are the register, bit 7 set makes the register address step up after each byte. Reads use a repeated start before the address with R/W = 1. Bytes go MSb first; a receiver may hold SCL low to make the sender wait.

CS low frames a transfer; SPC idles high. Data change on the falling edge of SPC and are sampled on the rising edge. A single read or write takes 16 clocks: bit 0 is R/W (1 read), bit 1 is MS (1 steps the address in multi-byte transfers), bits 2-7 are the register address, bits 8-15 the data byte, MSb first. Each further byte adds 8 clocks. On a read the part drives SDO from bit 8. Multi-byte reads also work in 3-wire mode.

operation.topic: Power-down, output data rate and one-shot
operation.text: After boot PD = 0 and the part is powered down; PD = 1 makes it active. ODR[2:0] picks 1, 7, 12.5 or 25 Hz for both pressure and temperature. With ODR = 000 the part waits in one-shot mode: writing ONE_SHOT = 1 in CTRL_REG2 takes one pressure and one temperature reading, after which the bit clears, the outputs hold the new data and STATUS_REG updates.

RES_CONF sets how many internal samples are averaged for each reading: 8 to 512 for pressure, 8 to 64 for temperature. At 1 Hz the supply current is 4 µA in low-resolution mode (RES_CONF = 04h) and 25 µA in high-resolution mode (the default 0Fh), where the noise is 0.01 hPa RMS. The low current and noise mode draws 4.5 µA: RES_CONF = 05h with FIFO_CTRL = DFh (FIFO Mean mode, 32 samples) and CTRL_REG2 = 50h (FIFO on, decimation on).

With BDU = 1 the output registers freeze from the first byte read until both upper and lower parts have been read, so one reading never mixes two samples. With BDU = 0 they update continuously. STATUS_REG updates every ODR cycle whatever BDU is.

BOOT = 1 copies the factory trim from non-volatile memory back into the trimming registers, taking 2.2 ms, then clears itself. SWRESET = 1 returns all registers to the power-on configuration in 4 µs and clears itself. When both are wanted, SWRESET goes first, then BOOT.

REF_P (08h to 0Ah) holds a 24-bit two's-complement reference subtracted from the reading for the threshold interrupt and for Autozero. Setting AUTO_ZERO copies the present reading into REF_P and from then on the output is the reading minus REF_P. RESET_AZ, self-clearing, resets the Autozero function; resetting REF_P sets the RPDS registers to their default value.
RPDS (39h, 3Ah) is a 16-bit two's-complement offset used for a one-point calibration once the part is on the board.

DIFF_EN = 1 turns on the differential-pressure computation; enable it after REF_P and THS_P are loaded. PH_E and PL_E raise an event when the difference goes above +THS_P or below -THS_P. With LIR = 0 the INT_DRDY output follows the event and reading INT_SOURCE has no effect on it; with LIR = 1 the event is latched in INT_SOURCE and the pin stays set until INT_SOURCE is read, which clears it.

INT_S[2:1] in CTRL_REG3 puts the pressure-high, pressure-low or either event on the pin, or, at 00, the data signals chosen in CTRL_REG4: data-ready, FIFO watermark, FIFO overrun or FIFO empty. INT_H_L sets active high or low and PP_OD push-pull or open drain.

P_DA and T_DA set when a new pressure or temperature sample arrives and clear when PRESS_OUT_H or TEMP_OUT_H is read. P_OR and T_OR set when a new sample lands while the previous flag was still set, and clear on the same reads.

A 32-slot FIFO holds pressure readings, so the host can sleep and read a burst later. FIFO_EN in CTRL_REG2 enables it and F_MODE[2:0] in FIFO_CTRL picks the mode. Bypass: unused and empty. FIFO: fills to 32 (or to the watermark when STOP_ON_FTH = 1) and stops. Stream: keeps the latest 32, dropping the oldest. Stream-to-FIFO: streams until a trigger event set in INTERRUPT_CFG, then fills and stops; set LIR = 1 for this. Bypass-to-Stream and Bypass-to-FIFO: idle until the IA flag in INT_SOURCE triggers Stream or FIFO operation. FIFO_STATUS gives the fill count and the watermark, overrun and empty flags, which can also drive INT_DRDY.

F_MODE = 110 uses the FIFO as a hardware moving average of 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32 pressure samples, set by WTM_POINT. With FIFO_MEAN_DEC = 0 the averaged output comes at the ODR; with 1 it is decimated, to 1 Hz at ODR codes 4 or 2 and to 1.04 Hz at ODR code 3. The FIFO contents cannot be read in this mode.

With the FIFO on, its samples come out through the pressure output registers 28h to 2Ah, oldest first, by single or burst reads. In a burst the address wraps from 2Ah back to 28h, so reading all 32 levels takes 96 bytes.
Registers 2Ch (high byte) and 2Bh (low byte) hold a 16-bit two's-complement temperature reading at 480 LSB/°C.

The HLGA package is ECOPACK, RoHS and Green compliant and qualified for soldering heat to JEDEC J-STD-020. The pin 1 indicator on the bottom is left unsoldered. ST's TN1198 gives surface-mount guidance for MEMS sensors in HLGA packages.
